newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Modelo Q1 could slip on lower volumes.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Modelo Q1 could slip on lower volumes.

text.p: Sales volumes will likely be flat and there is concern over operating margins, but top Mexican brewer Grupo Modelo SA will still post respectable first quarter results, analysts said.
Results due later this month are likely to show Modelo holding onto its dominant position in the Mexican beer market and continuing to show robust export growth.

"They're still the dominant factor in the market and exports continue to do great," analyst Scott Weiss of D.A. Campbell in Los Angeles told Reuters. "They'll continue to be the leader even though their stock has been hurt recently."
A Reuters survey of three beverage analysts predicted an increase in net income but a drop-off in gross and operating results.
The table shows an average of the analysts' Q1 1997 forecasts. To account for the impact of inflation, Q1 1996 results are adjusted upwards by March-on-March inflation of 24.45 percent.
Survey
Earnings per share 0.32 pesos 0.269 pesos
Net profit 263 million pesos 218 million pesos
Operating income 432 million pesos 535 million pesos

Gross profit 1.310 bln pesos 1.419 bln pesos
Gross margin 44.33 percent 46.8 percent
Revenue 2.959 bln pesos 3.033 bln pesos
Sales volume 6.78 million hctltrs 6.56 million hectoliters

One floor trader on the Mexican stock exchange said Modelo stock took a hit on Thursday on word that that first-quarter results would be lackluster. The C shares fell 2.40 pesos to 45.80 pesos on Thursday, but gained back 0.50 pesos o 46.30 by mid-day on Friday.

That concern likely was sparked by company indications that domestic sales volumes will be flat this quarter in what is being attributed to a sluggish consumer recovery. But overall volumes are predicted to rise on 20 percent export growth.
A brisk quarter will be needed to hold off competitor Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de SV (FEMSA), whose impressive Q4 results in 1996 upstaged Modelo.
Sales for both companies are seen picking up later in the year as consumers warm up to a recent price increases and as the Mexican economy recovers further.

One issue that could affect the results is whether Modelo decides to charge operating expenses from its new $356 million plant in Zacatecas state to the first quarter or the second quarter. Analysts said the company has not firmly indicated which way it will go.
Modelo, which built the plant with cash reserves, started operations late in the first quarter with the first beer for sale rolling off the line on March 14.

"The operating margin will be below our expectations, assuming that they don't charge some of the expenses from the Zacatecas plant to the first quarter," Marco Vera, an analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Mexico City, told Reuters. "If so, it could be lower."
One house predicted operating margin would tumble as far as 12.7 percent.
((--Dan Trotta, Mexico City newsroom, +525 728-9507))
